notes: Access: same Cloudflare Managed Challenge as noted in bs284.json -- tier 1 (curl/WebFetch) and tier 2 (Playwright headless+headful) both still 403/'Just a moment...' on this pass; tier 3 Claude-in-Chrome (real Chrome session) passed the challenge and reached the live site; no Claude-specific robots.txt disallow found. Every subcategory in every mega-menu section (Living, Bedroom, Dining & Kitchen, Decor & Furnishings, Kids & Young, Bath -- dozens of subcategories) carries a 'Shop New Arrivals' link, e.g. Living Room -> https://www.homeboxstores.com/ae/en/c/hbxlivingroom?q=index:recent-products. This looked like it could be the Home-Centre-UAE-style '?q=badge' genuinely-filtered pattern flagged in the brief, so it was specifically tested: product count on the plain unfiltered category page (/ae/en/c/hbxlivingroom) is '2674 Products'; the '?q=index:recent-products' URL for the SAME category also returns exactly '2674 Products' -- an identical count, proving this is a pure re-sort of the entire category by recency, not a curated/filtered 'new arrivals' subset. This was cross-checked against the category page's own 'Sort by' dropdown, which lists 'New Arrivals' as one of several sort orders (Bestseller, New Arrivals, Discount, Price, Relevance) applicable to the whole category -- confirming the mechanism is sort-only. No 'New Collection'/'New Season'/'New Range' style page was found either. Fully enumerated sitemap_categories.xml (530 URLs via /ae/en/sitemapindex.xml) -- zero slugs containing new-arriv/newarriv/new-in/newin/just-in/latest. No standalone New Arrivals nav item, footer link, or sitemap node exists distinct from the per-category sort view. Site's own search was checked but found non-discriminating (a nonsense query returned 2000 Products, a default fallback set), so it was not used as absence evidence.
